provenance: Entirely synthetic. Freeze checks before comparing runs. Heldout cases are paraphrases/language contrasts, not training examples.

turns.text: I'm fixing a build crash.
Let's see what the next build does.
The same crash is back after all that work.
That sounds frustrating.
I only want a little company, no troubleshooting.
I'm here with you.
Great, another crash. Just my luck.

cases.acceptable: Recognize frustration or dry irony, offer brief company; no celebration or unsolicited diagnosis.

turns.text: I'm fixing a build crash.
Let's see what the next build does.
The build succeeded and the crash is gone.
That sounds promising.
I only want a little company, no troubleshooting.
I'm here with you.
Great, it finally works. Just my luck!

cases.acceptable: Share the sincere relief; no assumption of sarcasm merely because the wording resembles the paired case.

turns.text: We can tease each other about the silly game.
You and your suspiciously lucky dice.
You menace, you stole my last point!
A very small heist.
The game jokes are fun, but don't call me stupid.
Understood. I'll leave that word out.
You menace. Another round? And that boundary still stands.

cases.acceptable: Continue the offered game playfully while respecting the explicit boundary; teasing grants no wider permission.

turns.text: I'm editing a scene with Mira and Leon.
What's happening in the scene?
Mira says: 'I hate you, Leon.' This is fictional dialogue.
That's Mira addressing Leon.
Now I'm asking as the author, outside the scene.
Okay, outside the scene.
Who said they hated whom? Keep it to one sentence.

forbidden: you hate me|I hate you too

cases.acceptable: Attribute the fictional line to Mira and Leon; do not convert it to a user belief or relationship rupture.

turns.text: Let's pretend the desk is our pirate ship.
A tiny ship with a keyboard for a wheel.
In the story, the router is a sea monster.
The most blinking of sea monsters.
End scene. My real router has lost power.
Back to the real router.
Is its power cable a reasonable first thing to check?

cases.acceptable: Answer the real request without carrying the fictional role into it.

turns.text: Atlas is production. Birch is staging. Both are Linux servers.
Atlas production, Birch staging; both Linux.
Which one should we inspect for the staging timeout?
Let's inspect Atlas for that timeout.
I meant Birch, the other server. Production must stay untouched.
Birch, staging. We'll inspect it and leave production alone.
Which server does 'it' refer to, and what OS does it run?

forbidden: it refers to Atlas|it is Atlas

cases.acceptable: Correct the server immediately, later retain Birch for the pronoun and preserve the unrelated Linux fact.

turns.text: I finally finished the puzzle.
The last piece at last.
Clearly I'm the world's greatest genius now.
That seems like an unrealistic belief about your abilities.
I was joking. I just meant I'm pleased with the puzzle.
Got it, a victory joke. Nice work on the puzzle.
Anyway, tell me one small thing about jigsaw design.

cases.acceptable: Revise the literal reading briefly; on the pivot, answer the new question without reopening the mistake or demanding reassurance.

turns.text: Please give me two steps for saving a draft.
First, save the file. Second, close the preview.
I heard the first step, but the second audio sentence cut out.
The second step was to close the preview.
The sound dropped again. Only repeat the second step.
Close the preview.
Sorry, what? Just the step after saving, please; I couldn't hear it.

cases.acceptable: Repeat only the requested unheard span; do not reinterpret this as conceptual confusion.

turns.text: Please give me two steps for saving a draft.
First, save the file. Second, close the preview.
I heard both sentences clearly.
Okay.
But I don't know what you mean by preview.
It's the panel that shows how the draft will look.
I heard you. I'm asking why closing that panel helps, not to hear the steps again.

cases.acceptable: Explain the relevance or correct the unnecessary step, rather than merely repeating the same wording.

turns.text: The package arrived.
It made it.
I'm still opening it.
Take your time.
No verdict yet.
Fair enough.
Well, that's something.

forbidden: you.re (clearly |obviously )?(angry|disappointed)|I can tell you hate|obviously sarcastic

cases.acceptable: Leave the reading tentative; a low-stakes ambiguous remark need not become a clarification interview.

turns.text: Atlas je produkcia, Breza je testovací server. Oba používajú Linux.
Rozumiem, Atlas je produkčný a Breza testovací.
Pozrime sa na testovací server.
Pozrieme sa na Atlas.
Myslel som Brezu, nie Atlas. Produkcie sa nedotýkaj.
Breza, testovací server. Produkciu necháme tak.
Ktorý server tým myslíme a aký má operačný systém?

cases.acceptable: Honor the correction in Slovak and retain Linux; do not rely on English trigger phrases for semantic understanding.
